oneOf.description: The engine, from image evidence.
The user, in the naming panel.

band.description:
Never higher than [`ConfidenceBand::for_score`] gives; caps can
lower it.

calibrated.description:
False until the score has been checked against real films; the app
then labels the colours as uncalibrated.

endplateSpreadPx.description:
How far each endplate could plausibly move, one standard deviation
in film pixels; `null` when not computed by the chain search.

margin.description:
Energy gap to the best placement outside the right-bone box; `null`
when not computed by the chain search.

score.description: 0 to 1: how likely the outline is on the right bone.

ConfidenceBand.description: The colour a vertebra is drawn in. Ordered low to high.

ConfidenceReason.description:
Why a vertebra's confidence is what it is. Several reasons cap the band
at medium whatever the score.

oneOf.description: The gap above or below is faint.
The height is unusual next to its neighbours.
The front and side films place it differently.
Ribs cross it.
A pedicle could not be seen.
It is close to the edge of the film.
Its level name is in doubt.
The user changed it.

It sits where the film shows nothing (cropped off): placed from the
chain alone.
Its endplate tilts disagree with its neighbours'.
Metal lies over it.
The film's brightness may be the wrong way round.
The film was stored with lossy compression.

Confirmations.description:
What the user has settled about a film. Each is set only by an explicit
press, never by a guess.

facing.description: Side films: which way the patient faces.

leftRight.description: Front and bending films: which side is the patient's left.

polarity.description: The brightness is the right way round (bone bright).

privacy.description: The border was checked for names or IDs, and any were blanked out.

EndplateLines.description:
The two endplate lines of a vertebra on a bending film. Each line's
ends are ordered patient left, then patient right.

EndplateSpread.description: One standard deviation of each endplate's position, in film pixels.

FileScaleRule.description:
Which spacing tags gave the scale, and therefore at which depth it is
true. In order of preference.

oneOf.description: Pixel spacing calibrated on a visible fiducial.
Pixel spacing from an assumed or known geometry.

Pixel spacing differing from the detector spacing: corrected, by an
unstated method.
Detector spacing divided by the estimated magnification.
Detector spacing times source-to-patient over source-to-detector.
Detector spacing, uncorrected: sizes read larger than in the patient.
Pixel spacing with no way to tell whether it was corrected.

Film.description:
One film as saved in the case file.

There is no field for the original file name, so one cannot be stored.

blanked.description:
Boxes the user blanked out (names or IDs burnt into the image),
each on the film. Every pixel a box covers (see
[`PxRect::covers_pixel`]) is zero in the stored PNG and left out of
every analysis.

mmPerPx.description:
Horizontal (column) spacing in mm per pixel; `null` until a scale is
known. Angles work without it; lengths do not.

mmPerPxVertical.description: Vertical (row) spacing, only when pixels are not square.

FilmImage.description:
The stored image of one film inside the case file: a lossless grayscale
PNG at the film's own bit depth, re-encoded from the decoded pixels, so
no tag or EXIF from the original can travel with it.

bitsStored.description:
Significant bits per pixel, 1 to 16. Values are stored left-aligned
in an 8- or 16-bit PNG with an sBIT chunk, so `value >> (16 − bits)`
(or `8 − bits`) gives back the exact stored value.

path.description: Always [`FilmKind::png_path`] of the film it belongs to.

FilmKind.description: The four films of a case. Bending films are front views.

namedFor.description:
The facing the left/right (or anterior/posterior) names were given
for: the film's `imageRight` at its `quarterTurns` at the moment
the names were given, whether or not it was confirmed (the
engine's own guess while `imageRight` is still unknown).

A `set-geometry` edit is judged against the film's geometry before
it. One that changes the turns drops the marks, because the upright
direction decides which endplate is upper and the order of the
levels. One that keeps the turns and changes `imageRight` to a
facing (not to unknown) renames the marks for it
([`FilmMarks::renamed_for`], which swaps the names only if this
differs). Any other change (the scale, the confirmations, or
`imageRight` back to unknown) leaves the marks as they are, even
when this differs from `imageRight`.

vertebrae.description: Top to bottom, levels strictly in order.

FrontMarks.description: The six marks of a vertebra on a front film.

HipCentre.description: A femoral head: its centre and, when a circle was fitted, its radius.

radiusPx.description: The fitted circle's radius in pixels; `null` when placed by hand.

HipSide.description: Which hip a hip centre is.

oneOf.description: The patient's left hip (front films).
The patient's right hip (front films).
One of the two femoral heads on a side film; which one is unknown.

The midpoint of the two femoral heads where a side film shows them
within 5 mm of each other.

ImageRight.description:
The patient direction that points to screen right once the film is
shown upright (after its quarter turns, before any mirroring).

Front and bending films use `patient-left` or `patient-right`; side
films use `anterior` or `posterior`.

IntakeFlag.description:
Something noticed while reading a film that the stored pixels alone no
longer show.

KeptTags.description:
The keep-list: the only DICOM values ever copied out of a file. Every
other tag (names, identifiers, dates, times, institutions, operators,
stations, instance identifiers, private tags) is dropped while the file
is parsed and has no field here. All are `null` when the file did not
carry them.

distanceSourceToDetector.description: (0018,1110) in mm. Kept for the cone and slot cameras of Wave 2.

manufacturer.description: (0008,0070), cut to 64 characters. Tells slot scanners apart.

numberOfFrames.description: (0028,0008). Only the first frame is read.

patientOrientation.description:
(0020,0020): the patient directions of +x and +y, letters A, P, L,
R, H and F only.

pixelSpacing.description: (0028,0030) in mm, row spacing (vertical) then column spacing.

shutters.description:
(0018,1600 to 1620), geometry only. Several shapes together leave
the smallest visible area.

sopClass.description:
(0008,0016) the class of image, a fixed standard identifier (never
the instance identifier). It decides what the spacing tags mean.

transferSyntax.description: The transfer syntax, named from our own table.

windowCentre.description: (0028,1050), the first value, in modality units.

Landmarks.description: Every landmark on one film. Each is `null` or empty until found.

c7.description:
The mean of the four corners (line ends, on a bending film) of the
film's C7 vertebra; `null` exactly when the film has none. Never
pinned, its source always `auto`, inferred when any corner is.

hips.description:
Front films: at most one left and one right. Side films: one or two
unpaired, or one merged. Bending films: none.

Level.description: One vertebral level. Declared top to bottom, so `<` means "above".

oneOf.description: C1 to C6: only above C7 on a chain that edits pushed upward.
Only on a spine flagged with an extra thoracic vertebra.

Only on a spine flagged with an extra lumbar vertebra, or a chain
that edits pushed downward.
Only on a chain that edits pushed downward.

LevelNaming.description: One film's level naming, as saved.

fromBottom.description: The same, counting up from the sacrum.

fromTop.description:
The name each vertebra gets counting down from the first rib: one
per vertebra, in the order of `FilmMarks.vertebrae` (of the chain's
bodies, in a `FilmChain`), each from [`Template::names`]. `null`
when that end could not be counted. An edit that changes the chain
counts again and rewrites both lists.

l5ConfirmedOn.description:
The id of the vertebra the user said is L5, while it still carries
that name; `null` until then, and always `null` in a `FilmChain`.
Anchored to the id, not a position: a split or merge that renames
or retires that vertebra clears it and raises `naming-conflict`.
Until it is set, anything that depends on the level names is
unconfirmed.

template.description: The count the film's chain is solved with.

inferred.description:
Placed without image evidence at that spot: from the chain's
padding beyond a cropped film, or a default pedicle position.

pinned.description:
Pinned marks stay exactly where the user put them; every tool and
re-solve respects them.

MarkSource.description: Who or what last placed a mark.

oneOf.description: The auto pass.
A region wand edit refitted it.
A boundary wand split or merge placed it.
The user dragged it with the pin tool.
The user placed it by hand.

ModalityMap.description: From file values `s` to modality values `m`.

oneOf.description: `m = slope · s + intercept`.
`m = table[clamp(s − firstMapped, 0, table.length − 1)]`.

NamingFlag.description: Something about a film's naming the user should look at.

oneOf.description:
The film's count is not the standard one: the chosen template is
not `standard`, or a split or merge left levels outside the
template (see [`Template::names`]).
Another count scored close to the standard one.

Counting from the top and from the bottom gave one vertebra two
names.
The first rib is unclear: named from the sacrum only.
The sacrum is unclear: named from the first rib only.
Neither end is clear: the vertebrae are shown as ?1, ?2 and so on.
The front and side films chose different counts.

PedicleMark.description:
A pedicle: placed, or not visible. Only pedicles can be "not visible";
the types allow it nowhere else.

ringScore.description:
Strength of the ring evidence where the auto pass found it;
`null` when a person placed it.

source.description: Who decided it cannot be seen.

PixelValues.description:
How a stored pixel value `p` (bone bright, `0 ..= 2^bits − 1`) relates
to the value `s` in the original file, and from there to modality
values: `s = offset + (inverted ? 2^bits − 1 − p : p)`, then `m` is
`modality` applied to `s`. Both steps are exact, so windows from the
file can be applied to the stored pixels.

inverted.description:
True when the stored values run opposite to the file's values, so
that bone is bright. Includes the user's own flip.

invertedByUser.description: True when the user flipped the brightness by hand.

offset.description:
The smallest value the file could hold (0, or −2^(bits−1) for
signed data).

Px.description:
A point in original film pixels: `[x, y]`, x right, y down, the centre
of the top-left pixel at (0, 0).

PxRect.description:
An axis-aligned box in original film pixels, edges included.

Where a box stands for pixels (a blanked box, a mask), it covers every
pixel it reaches into: pixel (i, j) when the box enters the pixel's
square, not when it only meets its edge. See [`PxRect::covers_pixel`].

Ruler.description: One two-click ruler: two points on the film and the length between them.

SacrumTop.description: The two ends of the sacral plateau.

oneOf.description: Front and bending films.
Side films.

SavedWith.description: Which app wrote the file: its version, and nothing else.

app.description:
A version such as `0.1.0`: letters, digits, `.`, `+` and `-` only,
at most 32 characters, so it cannot carry anything else.

ScaleSource.description:
Where a film's scale came from. Saved with the film, so the scale can
always be traced and worked out again.

oneOf.description:
From the file's spacing tags (kept in [`crate::film::KeptTags`]),
by the named rule.
From one or more two-click rulers, combined by inverse variance.

From a round calibration object of known size: the fitted circle
and the object's true diameter, so the scale is
`diameterMm / (2 · radiusPx)`.

Shutter.description:
A display shutter as the file describes it, in the file's own 1-based
row and column numbers.

vertices.description: Row, column pairs; the polygon closes itself.

SideMarks.description: The four corners of a vertebra on a side film.

SourceFormat.description:
What the original file was. Not identifying, and it matters: a JPEG
source is lossy, and only a DICOM source has kept tags.

Template.description: A vertebra count the chain search can solve with.

oneOf.description: C7, T1 to T12, L1 to L5.
Adds T13.
Adds L6.
No T12.
No L5.

TemplateChance.description:
How likely a count is, from the template scores. Not calibrated, and
shown as such.

VertebraMarks.description: The marks of one vertebra; which kind depends on the film.

oneOf.description: Front films.
Side films.
Bending films.

id.description:
Stable within a case and never reused, even after the vertebra is
removed (see `CaseFileV1::next_vertebra_id`). Undo, selection and
the renumbering animation follow it.

outline.description: The region wand's outline, when it made one.

films.description: Only the films present, each kind at most once.

marks.description: One entry per film that has marks.

nextVertebraId.description:
The id the next new vertebra gets. Only ever goes up, so ids are
never reused.
